verses.text: The word that came to Jeremiah from Yahweh, saying,
“Yahweh, the God of Israel, says, ‘Write all the words that I have spoken to you in a book.

For, behold, the days come,’ says Yahweh, ‘that I will turn again the captivity of my people Israel and Judah,’ says Yahweh. ‘I will cause them to return to the land that I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it.’”
These are the words that Yahweh spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.
For Yahweh says: “We have heard a voice of trembling, of fear, and not of peace.
Ask now, and see whether a man travails with child. Why do I see every man with his hands on his waist, as a woman in travail, and all faces are turned pale?
Alas! for that day is great, so that none is like it. It is even the time of Jacob’s trouble; but he shall be saved out of it.
It shall come to pass in that day, says Yahweh of Armies, that I will break his yoke from off your neck, and will burst your bonds; and strangers shall no more make them their bondservants;
but they will serve Yahweh their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up to them.

Therefore don’t you be afraid, O Jacob my servant, says Yahweh; neither be dismayed, Israel: for, behold, I will save you from afar, and your offspring  from the land of their captivity. Jacob shall return, and shall be quiet and at ease, and no one shall make him afraid.

For I am with you, says Yahweh, to save you; for I will make a full end of all the nations where I have scattered you, but I will not make a full end of you; but I will correct you in measure, and will in no way leave you unpunished.”
For Yahweh says, “Your hurt is incurable, and your wound grievous.
There is no one to plead your cause, that you may be bound up. You have no healing medicines.

All your lovers have forgotten you. They don’t seek you: for I have wounded you with the wound of an enemy, with the chastisement of a cruel one, for the greatness of your iniquity, because your sins were increased.
Why do you cry for your hurt? Your pain is incurable: for the greatness of your iniquity, because your sins were increased, I have done these things to you.

Therefore all those who devour you shall be devoured; and all your adversaries, everyone of them, shall go into captivity; and those who plunder you shall be plunder, and all who prey on you will I give for a prey.
For I will restore health to you, and I will heal you of your wounds,” says Yahweh; “because they have called you an outcast, saying, ‘It is Zion, whom no man seeks after.’”

Yahweh says: “Behold, I will turn again the captivity of Jacob’s tents, and have compassion on his dwelling places. The city shall be built on its own hill, and the palace shall be inhabited in its own place.
Out of them shall proceed thanksgiving and the voice of those who make merry. I will multiply them, and they shall not be few; I will also glorify them, and they will not be small.
Their children also shall be as before, and their congregation shall be established before me. I will punish all who oppress them.

Their prince shall be of themselves, and their ruler shall proceed from among them. I will cause him to draw near, and he shall approach to me; for who is he who has had boldness to approach to me?” says Yahweh.
“You shall be my people, and I will be your God.
Behold, Yahweh’s storm, his wrath, has gone out, a sweeping storm: it shall burst on the head of the wicked.
The fierce anger of Yahweh will not return, until he has executed, and until he has performed the intentions of his heart. In the latter days you will understand it.”

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks, and Jeremiah is told to *write*—to capture His word in a form that will outlast the moment of speaking. What a trust: a prophet's pen becoming the means by which God's voice reaches not just one generation but all who come after.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Write *all* the words He has spoken—not just the comforting ones, but also the hard ones of judgment and rebuke. The whole truth, preserved in ink, becomes our inheritance. A grandparent knows: the hardest words spoken in love often matter most.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will turn again the captivity"—not by erasing what was lost, but by restoring the exiles to the land promised to their fathers. The God who remembers His covenant also remembers those who have forgotten home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: These words concern *both* Israel and Judah—the northern and southern kingdoms that had split long ago. The Lord speaks of a future where His fractured people are gathered again, not as enemies but as one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A voice of trembling, not peace—the sound of a people gripped by fear. Yet the Lord *names* their terror not to shame them but to announce that He has heard it. Sometimes naming our fear is the first step toward the silence of His care.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The image is haunting: men contorted like women in labor, faces gone pale with anguish. It's the picture of a people wracked with suffering so deep they've become unrecognizable. Only when we see ourselves truly undone can God's healing begin.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "The time of Jacob's trouble"—a trial unmatched in its severity, yet *he shall be saved out of it*. The pattern is ancient: affliction is not the end but a threshold. The Lord delivers not from the outside but *through* the darkest hour.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The yoke is broken, bonds burst asunder—a picture as physical and real as the captivity itself. The Lord does not merely comfort the enslaved; He *undoes* enslavement. Strangers will no longer hold dominion.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will serve Yahweh their God, and David their king—the One whom Christ would fulfill. The promise looks not only backward to the kingdom of old but forward to the King who would reign in righteousness and grace.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Don't be afraid." The Lord does not say this because the danger has passed but because He will be present *through* it. He saves Jacob "from afar" and brings back the offspring from captivity—a God who reaches across distance and time itself to gather His own.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will make a full end of all the nations... but not of you." Even in judgment, the Lord's mercy is particular: He corrects His people in measure, never abandoning them. A parent may punish, but does not disown.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The hurt is *incurable*, the wound *grievous*—the Lord speaks the unbearable truth about their condition without flinching. Sometimes love means refusing false comfort and looking squarely at how broken we are.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: No one to plead their cause, no healing medicines—they are utterly alone in their distress. Yet this very desolation is the soil where only *God's* healing can take root, where no human remedy can steal the glory of what He alone will do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their lovers have forgotten them—the alliances and treaties they trusted have failed. The wound is *His*, given in judgment for increasing sin. Yet even the Lord's judgment is not abandonment; it is the hand of One who still holds them, still cares enough to wound.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "Why do you cry for your hurt?" The Lord does not say it harshly but with the clarity of one who sees the cause: their iniquity is great, their sins increased. Healing cannot come while we hide from the root; it begins when we stop pretending.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All who have devoured Israel will be devoured; plunderers will be plundered. The Lord does not allow cruelty to triumph forever. Justice is His, and He will settle the accounts on behalf of those who have suffered.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "I will restore health to you, and I will heal you"—the Lord's word *turns* now from diagnosis to cure. They had been called an outcast, a city no one seeks; now the Physician Himself comes. His presence is the medicine.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The captivity is turned again, and compassion is shown on the dwelling places—home is restored, not as memory but as concrete reality. The city rises on its hill again; the palace is inhabited. The Lord rebuilds not just stones but a people's life.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the ruins comes thanksgiving and the voice of those who make merry. The Lord does not restore a somber people to a joyless land but promises abundance and gladness—the joy of those who have been forgiven and reunited.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Children born, congregation established—the future is no longer barren. The Lord opposes all who would oppress them. A new stability settles over what was shattered, and the Lord Himself guards it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Their prince shall be of themselves, their ruler from among them—leadership is restored. Yet the most striking word: "Who is he who has had boldness to approach to me?" Only the one the Lord causes to draw near. Authority flows from intimacy with God.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "You shall be my people, and I will be your God." The covenant is renewed—not cancelled by their failure but restored after their repentance. The Lord speaks the words of a Bridegroom calling His beloved back home.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The storm is Yahweh's wrath, and it *has gone out* to burst upon the heads of the wicked. The promise of restoration is not made in a world where evil is tolerated but in one where it is finally, terribly judged.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "In the latter days you will understand it." Readers today hear an echo of this in their own waiting—how often the Lord's full purpose is concealed from us in the moment, revealed only in hindsight. Yet His fierce anger toward evil remains sure, even when we cannot yet see its end.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
